newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 22.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 22.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends ***********************************************
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

PARIS - French advertising agency Euro RSCG, a subsidiary of Havas, wins the European advertising account for Haagen-Dazs ice cream, but declines to disclose the value of the award. A pan-European campaign is to be launched before the end of this year.

WASHINGTON - U.S. President Bill Clinton accuses the fashion industry of promoting heroin use by young people and said it should not try to "glamorize addiction to sell clothes." He was attacking the so-called "heroin chic" approach that has been used in some fashion photography, in which models pose dazed as if under the influence of drugs.

BONN - The German advertising industry should have a new quality-control system for inspecting billboards in place by October, an industry watchdog group says. Advertising industry association Informationsgemeinschaft zur Feststellung der Verbreitung von Werbetraegern says the new system would entail visiting billboard sites to ensure they correspond with companies' advertising sales agreements.

LONDON - Independent media buyer CIA Group Plc says it has agreed to buy Scandinavian company MarMedia Group for a maximum 29.6 million stg ($48.7 million) in cash and shares. CIA says it will also buy the 50 percent of Norwegian company Media Marketing not owned by Marmedia.

BONN - German free newspapers posted moderate growth in ad income for the second year in a row in 1996, an industry association says. With a 3.2 percent climb in advertising income to 3.011 billion marks ($1.8 billion), the association of German advertising pages (BVDA) says the relatively slow expansion reflected the weakness of the country's retail market.
PARIS - Promotion by candidates for the upcoming French election has been short, poorly-financed and thin on interest, advertising industry specialists say. (Reuter)

NEW YORK - D'Arcy Masius Benton & Bowles Communications says its Japanese unit D'Arcy Masius Benton & Bowles/TAI was named advertising and marketing agency of record by General Motors Corp's General Motors Japan Cadillac unit.

LONDON - One of Britain's top advertising agency creative directors urges ad agencies to trust their instincts and stop relying on market research in devising ad campaigns. "If it feels good, do it. It would be nice to hear it more often in advertising, instead of, Have you researched that with 5,000 people," says Trevor Beattie, creative director of GGT Advertising.

LONDON - British retailers have finally realised that developing a strong brand image is as key to their success as traditional marketing and sales activities, says Mary Portas, a former marketing director of Harvey Nichols. By focusing on the development of a strong brand image, Harvey Nichols over recent years has successfully moved from a Yuppie image to that of an exclusive fashion store, says Portas.

MEXICO CITY - Mexico's Grupo Televisa SA unveils a massive restructuring plan to cut costs, spruce up its television programming and convince skeptics it will remain the Spanish-speaking world's leading media company. The plan calls for $270 million in cuts over the next three years through a combination of layoffs and belt-tightening moves.

LOS ANGELES - Times Mirror Co says advertising revenues for its newspaper publishing group for the five weeks ended May 4 increased 9.6 percent to $162.6 million from $148.4 million in the prior year.

SAN FRANCISCO - Microsoft Corp and Netscape Communications Corp are escalating efforts to move Internet software from simple Web browsers to so-called push technology that ends the need to surf the Web for information and allows users to poll Internet sites for updates. Both companies have announced partnerships for companies that want to publish directly on the Internet and corporate intranets, or self-contained company networks.

PARIS - French media company Pathe says it has bought the Voyage television channel from Landmark Communication Inc of the United States. Voyage television airs programmes exclusively on tourism and leisure and is seen in France and Europe as well as other parts of the world.

NEW YORK - Bloomberg LP says MSNBC's Desktop Video service would provide financial and business stories through Bloomberg News Service terminals. Bloomberg will feature daily audio reports from MSNBC Desktop Video and Bloomberg's main newsroom will have access to MSNBC Desktop Video's two private subscriber cable networks, MSNBC Professional and MSNBC Private Financial Network.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

WASHINGTON - Mattel Inc, the makers of the Barbie doll, introduces its newest creation -- a Barbie look-alike named Becky in a pink wheelchair. The $19.95 doll -- slim, busty and long-tressed like the rest of the Barbie family -- wears a blue-green denim skirt and jacket with matching shoes and headband and pink tights. Her pink wheelchair has wheels trimmed with iridescent mylar and comes with its own little backpack.

CAMDEN, New Jersey - Campbell Soup Company says it will sell its German-based Beeck-Feinkost GmbH chilled foods businesss to Gilde Buy-Out Fund, a Dutch venture capital firm. Campbell, which bought the privately held gourmet salad and deli products business in 1987, says the unit's 1996 sales were about $65 million.

ADELAIDE - The Australian wine industry says it is ripe for continued growth after new vineyard plantings and favourable late conditions produced a record premium crush. However, overall grape tonnages and yields are down on 1996 and a shortfall in red wine supplies is set to continue.

WELLINGTON - Kiwifruit New Zealand says it will appeal a High Court decision preventing it from marketing overseas-harvested fruit in foreign markets. Kiwifruit NZ is the operating name of the Kiwifruit Marketing Board.

NEW YORK - Gateway 2000 Inc, a direct marketer of personal computers, unveils a network PC that costs under $1,000 as part of a product line aimed at capturing a greater share of the corporate PC market.

MELBOURNE - Australia's Foster's Brewing Group Ltd says it does not know how the GMG Brands group would view their jointly owned British pub business. Grand Metropolitan Plc, an equal partner with Foster's in the Inntrepreneur Pub Co Ltd, plans to merge with brewer Guinness Plc to become GMG Brands, raising queries over the merged group's commitment to the pub chain.

WARSAW - New car sales in Poland grew 29.9 percent in January-April against the same period last year to 174,224 units, an independent car market monitoring agency, Samar, says in a report. Fiat topped the list of passenger car makers with 60,742 units sold and a 34.9 percent market share.
CONSUMER TRENDS:
PARIS - A French court orders SNCF French railways to pay two anti-smoking groups 5,000 francs ($870) each in damages for its failure to crack down on smokers in a Paris train station.
(Reuter)

LONDON - Continued high occupancy levels and average room rates for hotels across Europe will cause a flurry of joint ventures, mergers and acquisitions as international hotel chains vie for dominance, a survey by consultants Arthur Andersen shows. London hotels outperformed all the other major cities in Europe in 1996 with an average room occupancy rate of 84.3 percent, says the survey.
PARIS - French coffee consumption is expected to fall in 1997, mostly the result of higher retail prices, the chairman of the French coffee industry and trade association says.

Consumption rose three percent last year and was broadly stable for the first three months of 1997 but consumers should start feeling the pinch of higher retail prices by the end of June, says Jean-Claude Frankel.
